evidence.finding_1_all_production_email_is_redire: EMAIL_OVERRIDE is provisioned for 'Preview, Production' (verified: npx vercel env ls production), and src/lib/email.ts:94 does 'const recipient = override || to' with NO NODE_ENV/VERCEL_ENV gate — directly contradicting the comment two lines above (:88 'In production, always send to the real recipient'). Consequence: every outbound production email (seller 30-day reminders, buyer inquiry notifications, alert matches, brand-request mail) goes to a single override inbox, with the real address only echoed into the subject line (:102). Sellers never receive reminders, buyers never receive replies, and one inbox accumulates other people's PII plus live 72h markSold action tokens that are not single-use.
evidence.finding_2_middleware_never_runs_in_produ: The intended deny-by-default session gate DOES NOT EXECUTE. Root cause: middleware.ts sits at the REPO ROOT while the app lives in src/app — Next requires src/middleware.ts when a src directory is used, so the file is silently ignored. Two independent proofs: (a) the production build log's route table lists all 42 routes but contains NO 'ƒ Middleware' entry, which Next always emits when middleware compiles; (b) unauthenticated GETs of nonexistent paths return 404, not the 307-to-/login that authorized() would force — /zzz-does-not-exist, /admin/zzz-nope and /totally/fake/path all 404. src/auth.config.ts:31-38 authorized() is therefore dead code and PUBLIC_PATHS is fiction. Nothing is exposed TODAY because every protected surface carries its own auth() guard (admin and seller via layout.tsx, /account/* per-page, all 9 API routes) — two API routes even comment 'Defense-in-depth', showing the author believed middleware was the primary gate. The defect is the total loss of defense-in-depth: any page or route added tomorrow without an explicit guard ships PUBLIC by default.
evidence.finding_3_preview_shares_the_production_: DATABASE_URL is provisioned for 'Production, Preview' (verified: vercel env ls), so preview deployments read and write the live production database.
evidence.verified_ok: Prod deployment matches HEAD (sha 56766d5). All required prod env vars present (24 project vars). evidence.totals: 11 vulnerabilities: 2 critical, 5 high, 4 moderate. fixAvailable: true for every one.
evidence.critical: next-auth 5.0.0-beta.31 (DIRECT dep) carries the Auth.js advisory 'configuration errors can cause existence-based auth checks to fail open'. Directly implicated here: src/auth.config.ts:37 is precisely an existence-based check (return !!auth). Also 'email normalizer validates the address before Unicode normalization, allowing a homoglyph @ bypass' — relevant because the domain guard at src/auth.ts:28 is an endsWith('@hellosugar.salon') string check. @auth/core <=0.41.2 shares the advisory cluster.
evidence.high: next 15.5.20 (DIRECT) — 8 advisories including 'unauthenticated disclosure of internal Server Function endpoints' (matches the observed action-id exposure), cache confusion of response bodies, SSRF in rewrites, unbounded Server Action payload, DoS via Server Actions, DoS via SVG image optimization. Plus @auth/drizzle-adapter <=1.11.2 (DIRECT), postcss, sharp, brace-expansion.

failures.proposed_fix: npm audit fix for the transitive set (postcss, sharp, brace-expansion, @auth/core). Upgrade direct deps deliberately: next-auth off 5.0.0-beta.31 (clears both criticals including the fail-open advisory this codebase's !!auth gate is exposed to), @auth/drizzle-adapter >1.11.2, next past the advisory range. vercel.json pins installCommand 'npm install --legacy-peer-deps', so re-verify peer resolution after the auth bump.

failures.orchestrator_verification: Mechanism CONFIRMED in source (src/auth.ts:62 returns the session object wholesale). The live payload could NOT be re-observed at merge time because the supplied cookie had stopped authenticating (/api/auth/session now returns null); the auditor's captured payload contained data far too specific to be fabricated.

evidence.method: GET with User A's own cookie
evidence.expected_response: Auth.js default shape: { user: { name, email, image }, expires }
evidence.actual_response: The raw database session row plus the entire user record — sessionToken IN CLEARTEXT, userId, emailVerified, role, sellerAccess, createdAt, loginCount, lastLoginAt, ownerIdentifier, ownerLinkSource.
evidence.why_it_matters: The session cookie is correctly __Secure-prefixed and HttpOnly, but this endpoint hands the same token value back in a JavaScript-readable JSON body, defeating HttpOnly for token theft — and next.config.ts:15 ships script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' (DEBT-025), so any injected inline script can fetch('/api/auth/session') and exfiltrate a token valid for 30 days.
evidence.cause: The session callback at src/auth.ts:45-63 ends in 'return session', returning the adapter's merged object rather than a whitelisted projection, so every DB column on both the session and user rows is serialized.
evidence.related: The EMAIL_OVERRIDE defect is also a PII-misdelivery issue — seller names, listing titles, buyer inquiry messages and phone numbers all route to one unintended inbox in production.
evidence.verified_ok: No cross-origin read of this data (no Access-Control-Allow-Origin granted to a foreign origin on any endpoint tested). Buyer-facing listing queries do not select owner contact PII. Owner-directory PII is admin-gated behind requireAdmin(). No PII observed in any logged-out response across 18 pages and 6 API routes.

failures.proposed_fix: In the session callback, build and return an explicit projection: assign only session.expires and session.user = { id, name, email, image, role, sellerAccess, ownerIdentifiers }. Never let sessionToken, userId, loginCount, lastLoginAt, createdAt, ownerLinkSource or emailVerified reach the response. Separately retire 'unsafe-inline' from script-src (DEBT-025) so an XSS cannot reach this endpoint.
failures.reproduce: curl -s https://marketplace.hellosugar.salon/api/auth/session -H 'Cookie: __Secure-authjs.session-token=<valid-session>'   # needs a FRESH cookie; the audit cookie has since stopped authenticating

evidence.drift_1: globals.css --hs-taupe / --hs-color-text-muted = #755B54 vs tokens.json color.text-muted = #8F7067 (the file's own comment concedes the deviation, made for accessibility reasons).
evidence.drift_2: globals.css --radius-lg = 0.75rem (12px) and --radius-xl = 1rem (16px) vs tokens.json radius.lg = 16px and radius.xl = 24px — the app's radius scale is shifted down one step from the source of truth.

failures.proposed_fix: Either adopt the generated variables.css/tailwind-preset.js directly (updating the Tailwind v4 @theme wiring to reference them), or keep the hand-port and add a CI check that diffs globals.css's hex and radius values against tokens.json so drift is caught automatically instead of relying on a comment.
failures.reproduce: Diff the hex/radius values in src/app/globals.css against the brand skill's tokens/tokens.json — text-muted and the radius scale will not match.

evidence.finding: Repo root carries ~2,566 lines across 8 stray planning/audit markdown files (TECHNICAL_DEBT.md 822, research.md 914, PROJECT_PLAN.md 254, HS_Marketplace_Plan_of_Attack.md 188, plan.md 158, audit-report.md 101, progress.md 89, discovery.md 40) plus audit-report.json and an empty .tmp_review/ — committed working notes from prior AI-assisted sessions, not app documentation.

failures.proposed_fix: Move planning/audit scratch docs into docs/archive/ or a separate notes repo and delete the empty .tmp_review/. Keep only README.md and TECHNICAL_DEBT.md (if DEBT- tickets are actively tracked) at the root.
failures.reproduce: ls *.md at repo root; ls -la .tmp_review (0 entries)

failures.check: Lint and format are clean and enforced

evidence.finding: npx eslint . runs clean (0 errors) but leaves 29 warnings (unused vars, missing react-hooks/exhaustive-deps, instead of next/image). ci.yml's own comment acknowledges the backlog and deliberately omits --max-warnings=0, so the count can grow indefinitely without failing CI. Related: next.config.ts:37-42 sets typescript.ignoreBuildErrors AND eslint.ignoreDuringBuilds, so nothing gates the build itself — CI's separate 'npx tsc --noEmit' and 'npx eslint .' steps are the only gate, and both currently pass.

failures.proposed_fix: Set a --max-warnings ratchet in CI (start at 29, lower over time) so new warnings fail the build while the historical backlog stays. Remove ignoreBuildErrors/ignoreDuringBuilds from next.config.ts now that tsc and eslint are green, so the build itself gates again.

na.reason: Not conclusively gradable with the supplied inputs. User A was established as an ADMIN before probing (role=admin, sellerAccess=true), so any successful cross-user read is legitimate org-wide access, not IDOR. No User B resource IDs were supplied and none could be discovered — the only listing in the system is User A's own draft, and authenticated /admin/listings and /admin/queue payloads contained zero other listing ids or sellerIds. Write-side probes were out of bounds (production, real data). Static review found NO ownership gap: /api/listings filters strictly on eq(listings.sellerId, session.user.id) with no admin bypass branch (behaviorally confirmed — the admin session saw only its own listing); listings actions enforce sellerId !== user.id && role !== 'admin' before every mutation; alerts/favorites/saved-competitors/contact constrain by session.user.id; all admin and owner-directory/mapping actions call requireAdmin(); all 7 audited [id] pages carry the guard. RE-RUN with a non-admin User A cookie plus at least one User B listing id.

No way to read GCP IAM from this environment. The app's BigQuery identity was determined (hs-marketplace@even-affinity-388602.iam.gserviceaccount.com — client_email only, key material never read), but gcloud is not installed and the available BigQuery MCP authenticates as the human user rather than the app service account, so granted roles cannot be enumerated. Needs 'gcloud projects get-iam-policy even-affinity-388602' to confirm the SA holds only BigQuery Data Viewer + Job User on the specific datasets. Same gap applies to Boulevard, Monday.com, GITHUB_DISPATCH_TOKEN and internal-KPI credentials. Positive: src/lib/bigquery/client.ts is import 'server-only', prod reads inline JSON from GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON (never a file path), the real key is absent from the deployed bundle and build output, and .secrets/ is gitignored and untracked.

Requires state-changing writes against production (submit listing for review, admin approve/reject, status change) — withheld by instruction. Read-only portions were traversed and worked: wizard intro gating, listing detail, edit page load, admin queue/listings tables. IMPORTANT: the 2026-07-06 audit's Blocker on this flow (wizard could not advance past Financials) appears FIXED in source — stepSchemas plus per-step safeParse replaced the .and() intersection (src/lib/listings/schemas.ts:96; src/components/listings/ListingWizard.tsx:70-88) — but this was NOT confirmed end-to-end live and should be the first thing re-tested on staging.

Verifying real action feedback (after Submit for Review, or admin approve/reject) requires a state-changing write against production; not executed. Only the pre-submit pattern was observed — a disabled 'Continue to Form' button that unlocks after the fee-structure checkbox — which works as designed.

na.check: No race conditions or stale-state UI
na.reason: Rapid repeat-click and multi-tab overlapping-fetch scenarios were not exercised against this production instance within budget. No such issues were observed incidentally during normal navigation, which is not a substitute for the targeted behavioral test.
DevTools network throttling / offline simulation mid-form-fill was not run within budget.

out_of_scope_observations.note: Page <title> is a generic 'Hello Sugar Marketplace' on several inner pages (/account/alerts, /seller/listings/[id], /seller/listings/[id]/edit, /admin/listings) rather than page-specific.
MapTiler console warning on /browse: style 'Streets Default v2' is deprecated and will be removed — migrate before it breaks.
/seller/listings redirects straight to a single-listing detail page when the seller has exactly one listing, skipping the index UI entirely — confirm this is intended.
GET / and GET /browse return HTTP 200 while logged out and only redirect via a streamed RSC NEXT_REDIRECT, so an unauthenticated visitor briefly renders the /browse skeleton before landing on /login.

The /browse map does not degrade gracefully: with WebGL2 unavailable it throws and takes the ENTIRE page down to a 'Something went wrong' error boundary instead of falling back to the list view. Observed when a Lighthouse run passed --disable-gpu; the console error is 'Graphic rendering with WebGL2 has been disabled or is not supported by your graphic card.' Worth fixing independently of scoring — staff on locked-down or older devices would lose the whole page.

Evidence behind the performance PASS (Lighthouse 13.4.1, simulated throttling): /login desktop Perf 85-87, / desktop Perf 90, FCP 0.4s, LCP 1.0s, TBT 230-320ms, Speed Index 0.8-1.2s; mobile medians Perf ~80-88, LCP 3.0-4.3s. CLS 0.000-0.029 on EVERY run. Server response 50-70ms, total weight 449-482 KiB. Two catastrophic mobile samples carried Lighthouse's own 'tested device has a slower CPU than expected' warning and are host noise. Also flagged: unused-javascript 83-107 KiB, and unsized-images on hs-logo-horizontal-color.png / hs-logo-drop.png. GAP: no valid measurement of authenticated /browse (the one run that reached it hit the WebGL error boundary above, and the session died before a redo) — re-confirm there with a fresh token.
A cross-origin Server Action POST returns a bare HTTP 500 with an opaque digest rather than a 403 — correct security outcome, poor failure surface.

The GitHub repo Hello-Brands/HS-Marketplace is PUBLIC (githubRepoVisibility: public in deployment metadata) for an internal tool. No secrets are tracked (verified: only .env.example), so this is not a leak, but source visibility for an internal app deserves a deliberate decision.
All 24 server-action ids ship in the unauthenticated client bundle with readable names — inherent to Next.js, but it is what made the unguarded getListings hole discoverable.

DEBT-025 (permissive CSP), DEBT-028 (in-memory rate limiting) and DEBT-017 (action tokens not single-use) are all referenced in code comments as still open.
All logo usages are raster PNG; the vector hs-logo.svg ships in public/ but is never referenced in src — brand guidance prefers SVG where vector works.
The login button's focus ring uses --color-hs-red-500 (#EF3059) rather than the exact --hs-color-focus (#ED1845) token; visible and crimson-family, so not failed, but worth aligning.
